sentences.text: Dated : 12-03-2025  Shri Sankalp Kochar- learned counsel for the appellant.

Shri G.S. Thakur- Government Advocate for the responden Heard on I.A. No.18317/2024, which is fifth application under Section 389 (1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on behalf of appellant -Nagendra Sing @ Bhaiyan.
His earlier four applications for suspension of sentence have been dismissed as withdrawn by this Court.

The appellant has been convicted by First Additional Sessions Judge, Amarpatan, District Satna in Special Trial No.120/2017 vide judgment dated 12.10.2018 for the offences under Sections 376(2n)
and 506-II of IPC and sentenced to undergo life imprisonment with fine of Rs.5,000/- and R.I. for 5 years with fine of Rs.1000/- respectively with default stipulations.

entities.text: First Additional Sessions Judge, Amarpatan, District Satna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The prosecution story found to be proved in short is that on 25.02.2017 at about 08:00 PM the prosecutrix left the house to attained the nature of call, the appellant came their and took her away and committed rape with her repeatedly without her consent by giving threat to kill her.
On this finding the appellant has been convicted and sentenced for the offence, as mentioned above.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that he has been falsely implicated in the case.
The appellant was having previous enmity with the 2 CRA-8466-2018 father of the prosecutrix who has been convicted for the offence under Section 376 of IPC.
It is also submitted that the appellant has already undergone more than 8 years of the jail sentence imposed by the trial Court.
There is lot of improvement in the version of the prosecutrix since the beginning.
FSL report Ex.-P/14 is also negative.
This appeal is of the year 2018 and there is no possibility of early hearing of the appeal in near future.

He is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by the directions and conditions,
which may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, it is prayed that the application for suspension of sentence may be allowed.

sentences.text: Learned Government Advocate for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer for suspension of sentence and submitted as per the MLC report there are external or internal injuries were found on the private parts of the prosecutrix, therefore, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be dismissed.
Heard learned counsel for both the parties and perused the record.

Considering the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the fact that the FSL report is negative and the appellant has already undergone more than 8 years of the jail sentence, the application for suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, 18317/2024, is allowed.

It is directed that substantive jail sentence of appellant - Nagendra Singh @ Bhaiyan shall remain suspended subject to his depositing the fine amount (if not already deposited) and on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in 3 CRA-8466-2018 the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court on 28.04.2025 and on all other subsequent dates as may be fixed by the Court concerned in this behalf.
List the matter for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
(SUSHRUT ARVIND DHARMADHIKARI)

(ANURADHA  JUDGE JUD  AL Nagendra Singh @ Bhaiyan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199296526/
